blocks.task_summary: Find the distance BV between points B(6,8,0) and V(3,4,9) in the 3D pyramid.

evidence.basis: (6−3)² + (8−4)² + (0−9)² (A1); 10.3 (= √106) A1. Note: SC(A0)A1 for vector misinterpretation.

blocks.task_summary: Find the size of angle BVC at vertex V in the pyramid using vector dot product or cosine rule.
method_path: Form vectors VB = ⟨3, 4, −9⟩ and VC = ⟨3, −4, −9⟩ from coordinates
accepted_alternatives: METHOD 1 (cosine rule): Note BV = VC = √106 and BC = 8, then apply cosine rule cos(BVC) = (BV² + VC² − BC²) / (2·BV·VC) = (106 + 106 − 64) / (2·106) = 148/212 = 74/106 → BVC ≈ 0.798
METHOD 2 (midpoint): Let M be midpoint of BC, BM = 4, then BVC = 2·arcsin(4/√106) ≈ 2·0.399018 ≈ 0.798

evidence.basis: METHOD 1: (A1) BV = VC AND BC = 8, (M1) attempt cosine rule, (A1) correct substitution, A1 for BVC = 0.798 (45.7°).
METHOD 3: (A1) vectors VC = ⟨3,−4,−9⟩ and VB = ⟨3,4,−9⟩, (M1) attempt cosine formula, (A1) cos(BVC) = 74/106, A1 for BVC = 0.798 (45.7°).
